label: History
sources: Live free-tier lessons, History AQA (8145): Conflict and tension 1918-1939, lesson 7 'The Collapse of the League: Manchuria and Abyssinia' (text, recall card, knowledge checks, 4-mark source question and mark scheme). Teacher-screen names, classes and figures are made up.

lesson.title: The Manchurian Crisis
lesson.body: In September 1931 an explosion damaged the South Manchurian Railway near Mukden. Japan blamed Chinese soldiers and used the explosion as an excuse to invade Manchuria. China asked the League of Nations for help.

flash.model: The League of Nations' 1932 report on Manchuria. It found Japan's invasion was not self-defence.

practice.question: What was the Mukden Incident of September 1931?
options: A Chinese invasion of Japanese territory in Korea
A staged explosion on the railway, used by Japan as an excuse to invade
A League of Nations attack on Japanese ships
A border clash between Japan and the Soviet Union
practice.feedback: Right. Japan staged it, then blamed China.

practice.question: The 1932 League report on Manchuria, which found Japan in the wrong, was the _____ Report.

source.label: Source A
source.caption: From the Lytton Report, October 1932.
source.text: ‘The military operations of the Japanese troops on the night of 18-19 September 1931 cannot be regarded as measures of legitimate self-defence. The recently established Manchukuo regime cannot be regarded as having resulted from a genuine and spontaneous independence movement; it is an instrument of Japanese policy.’

exam.question: Using Source A, identify two findings of the Lytton Report.
exam.answer: It found that Japan's military action in September 1931 was not legitimate self-defence, and that the new state of Manchukuo was not a genuine independence movement but a tool of Japanese policy.
exam.well: Two findings, each clear and precise.
exam.next: Say what the League did with the report next.

q1.question: Why did the League's sanctions on Italy in 1935 fail to stop Mussolini?
options: Italy had already left the League
Sanctions left out oil, coal and steel
why: Not quite. Italy was still in the League.
The sanctions left out oil, coal and steel,
and the Suez Canal stayed open.

q2.question: The secret 1935 plan to give Mussolini most of Abyssinia was the _____-Laval Pact.
q2.right: Right. Britain's Hoare and France's Laval.
